Physical fabrication, component integration, and food-service review
Functional integration, aesthetic redesign discussion, and V1 scope resolution

requirements.title: Dual Independent Mixing Stations
requirements.definition: The prototype must provide two mixing stations that can operate together while retaining independent station control.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers station count and operational independence only; speed behavior, mixing quality, and dispensing are separately testable Requirements.

requirements.title: Smooth Frothy Matcha Mixing
requirements.definition: Each station must mix fine matcha powder into a smooth, consistent, well-aerated beverage comparable to handheld electric frothers.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines the observable beverage result; motor speed and whisk hardware remain separate mechanisms that can be modified independently.

requirements.title: Independent Variable-Speed Motor Drive
requirements.definition: Each mixing station must have an independently adjustable motor drive with sufficient torque and a usable speed range for slow mixing and higher-speed frothing.
requirements.boundary_note: Motor maximum speed, torque, shaft characteristics, and station speed range are attributes of one drive mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Matcha-Compatible Whisk Configuration
requirements.definition: The whisk head, material, size, shaft attachment, and operating depth must suit fine-powder matcha, the selected bowls, and the desired foam quality.
requirements.boundary_note: Groups tightly coupled whisk-performance parameters; quick removal is separate because it can change without changing whisking geometry or material.

requirements.title: Quick Whisk Removal
requirements.definition: Whisks must detach quickly, preferably without tools, to support cleaning, replacement, and bowl removal.
requirements.boundary_note: Removal usability is independently actionable from whisk mixing performance and bowl-removal geometry.

requirements.title: Small Bowl Capacity and Form
requirements.definition: The stations must use relatively small, deep bowls matching the earlier visual proportions rather than large eight-quart vessels.
requirements.boundary_note: Capacity, depth, and visual bowl proportions form one vessel-selection mechanism; removability is independently specified.

requirements.title: Quick Bowl Removal and Swapping
requirements.definition: Bowls must lift out and reconnect easily so pre-prepared bowls can be swapped quickly and cleaned between uses.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers bowl detachment and reconnection; bowl capacity and whisk detachment can evolve separately.

requirements.title: Splash-Free Mixing Operation
requirements.definition: Mixing must minimize splashing and mess across the supported speed range through positioning, bowl geometry, speed control, or a guard when necessary.
requirements.boundary_note: Splash containment has its own acceptance outcome and can fail even when speed adjustment and mixing quality work.

requirements.title: Low Noise and Vibration
requirements.definition: The device must avoid excessive operational noise, vibration, and rattling during repeated event use.
requirements.boundary_note: Noise and vibration are an independently testable event-use constraint rather than an attribute of visual appearance.

requirements.title: Controlled Button-Operated Dispensing
requirements.definition: Each station must dispense on demand through a simple button-operated valve, producing a smooth controlled stream without abrupt release or closed-valve dripping while preserving beverage consistency.
requirements.boundary_note: Valve control and flow behavior form one dispensing mechanism; spout appearance, plumbing leakage, and spout removal have separate outcomes.

requirements.title: Spout Geometry and Orientation
requirements.definition: Custom spouts must resemble the selected rendering, face the barista, and direct the beverage downward into cups in a way that preserves consistency.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers physical spout shape, direction, and operator orientation; valve behavior and leak prevention are independently testable.

requirements.title: Leak-Free Plumbing and Liquid Containment
requirements.definition: Bowl outlets, fittings, valves, tubing, and seals must prevent leaks or seepage, keep liquid out of the base and electronics, and remain dry during operation.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns containment failures such as cracked fittings and leakage; controlled pour rate and sanitation remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Removable Spouts
requirements.definition: The custom spouts must be readily removable for cleaning, flushing, and replacement.
requirements.boundary_note: Spout detachment is independently changeable from the integrated plumbing-cleaning procedure and dispensing behavior.

requirements.title: Food-Safe Contact Materials
requirements.definition: All beverage-contact parts must use appropriate food-safe materials such as stainless steel and food-grade silicone.
requirements.boundary_note: Material suitability is independent from whether the same components are easy to clean or service.

requirements.title: Sanitary and Cleanable Fluid Path
requirements.definition: The integrated bowl-to-spout fluid path must be flushable and serviceable, avoid inaccessible liquid traps, and support routine sanitation of residue from matcha and milk.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers sanitation of the integrated path; quick removal of bowls, whisks, and spouts remains with those independently evolving components.

requirements.title: Stable and Durable Structure
requirements.definition: The prototype must remain sturdy and stable during operation and repeated event use without rattling, shifting, or excessive tower movement.
requirements.boundary_note: Structural rigidity is independently verifiable from noise level, enclosure size, and platform cup clearance.

requirements.title: Raised Cup-Clearance Platform
requirements.definition: A separate fitted platform must raise the mixer enough for standard 12-ounce cups to sit below the low-mounted spouts, with the mixer fitting edge-to-edge on top.
requirements.boundary_note: Platform height, footprint, and mixer fit form one functional support mechanism; its logo and colors belong to visual-design Requirements.

requirements.title: Compact Enclosure Proportions
requirements.definition: The machine enclosure should retain practical, visually balanced proportions and avoid unnecessary bulk while accommodating the required plumbing and controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Enclosure dimensions can be accepted or modified independently from its colors, branding, and structural rigidity.

requirements.title: Maintenance and Service Access
requirements.definition: Motors, electronics, plumbing, and other internals must remain accessible through removable or openable enclosure sections for adjustment, repair, and replacement.
requirements.boundary_note: Service access is distinct from routine food-path cleaning and from quick operator removal of bowls, whisks, or spouts.

requirements.title: Standard 120V Wall Power
requirements.definition: The first prototype must operate from a standard 120V wall outlet, with battery operation left for a possible later version.
requirements.boundary_note: External power-source choice is separate from internal supply capacity and the user-facing power switch.

requirements.title: Adequate Electrical Power Capacity
requirements.definition: The power supply and motor controllers must safely support both motors, valves, fans, and expected load with reserve capacity to avoid overload or overheating.
requirements.boundary_note: Power rating and thermal margin are one electrical-capacity mechanism; wall input and switch placement are independently selectable.

requirements.title: Main Power Interface
requirements.definition: The machine must include a functional, accessible main power control integrated into the central front control area.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns power on/off behavior and physical control placement; lighting and cosmetic styling of the control are separate.

requirements.title: Premium DJ-Style Visual Identity
requirements.definition: The machine and platform should be visually engaging, fun, premium, and recognizably inspired by DJ turntables for events and social-media use.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines the overall visual acceptance criterion; color, branding, lighting, and decorative control details can each evolve independently.

requirements.title: Beige and Green Color Scheme
requirements.definition: The enclosure and platform must use the selected beige treatment with coordinated green accents and matching detail colors.
requirements.boundary_note: Color selection is independently modifiable from logos, lighting, and the overall DJ-style form.

requirements.title: Machine Branding and Placards
requirements.definition: The mixer and platform must carry the client-selected Karla's Matcha Mixer branding, fonts, logos, and placard placement so branding is visible from relevant customer and barista viewpoints.
requirements.boundary_note: Text, logo, font, and placard placement are one branding mechanism; decorative controls and illumination remain separate.

requirements.title: DJ-Style Control Detailing
requirements.definition: Visible controls and surrounding graphics should recreate the rendering's DJ-booth details, including silver-style knobs, Deck labels, measurement markings, and selected K button markings.
requirements.boundary_note: Groups the coordinated rendering-style control graphics and decorative hardware; actual control behavior and LED illumination are separate.

requirements.title: Decorative LED Lighting
requirements.definition: The visual design should include suitable LED lighting around selected elements such as bowls, the base, or the power control to strengthen the rendering-inspired event appearance.
requirements.boundary_note: Lighting can be sourced, implemented, or deferred independently from control styling, branding, and core functionality.

requirements.title: System Layout and CAD Design
requirements.definition: The freelancer must develop and refine the mechanical system layout and CAD design needed to place the selected components and fabricate the prototype.
requirements.boundary_note: CAD and physical layout are a distinct design artifact; parts selection and electrical wiring documentation have separate acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Component Selection and Bill of Materials
requirements.definition: The freelancer must select compatible prototype components and provide an updated bill of materials reflecting approved engineering changes.
requirements.boundary_note: BOM completeness and component compatibility form one engineering deliverable; actual product behaviors remain owned by their functional Requirements.

requirements.title: Electrical Wiring Plan
requirements.definition: The freelancer must provide a basic wiring plan or electrical overview for the motors, controllers, valves, fans, power supply, and controls.
requirements.boundary_note: The wiring plan is an independently requested technical artifact rather than a generic implementation or testing activity.

requirements.title: Engineering Documentation Archive
requirements.definition: Project engineering records such as CAD files, material information, BOM data, wiring information, and other useful maintenance documentation should be retained for future development.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers preservation and future availability of the documentation set, not the creation criteria of the individual CAD, BOM, or wiring artifacts.

requirements.title: Simple Off-the-Shelf V1 Approach
requirements.definition: The first prototype should use the simplest reliable and cost-effective engineering approach, relying on off-the-shelf components where practical while allowing necessary custom fabrication.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a temporary prototype-engineering constraint rather than a Family-level substitute for the individual product behaviors.

unresolved_candidates.description: The history may establish a distinct task-local obligation to ship the prototype in its current functional state with the raised base and unused materials, but it is unclear whether this should be represented as an independent delivery Requirement or treated as project administration around the underlying prototype deliverables.
A future magnetic-stirrer version is discussed, but the client does not clearly assign that future redesign to the freelancer within the current project scope.
